assignedReviews.card_evidence: When resistors are in series (in a row), you add their resistances to get the total, then apply Ohm's law.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a series-resistance rule and Ohm's law, which is background knowledge for understanding circuits, but it does not involve a guided investigation, varying loads/battery, or inferring the current-voltage-resistance relationship as the competency requires.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When resistors are in series (in a row), you add their resistances to get the total, then apply Ohm's law.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw diagrams of and assemble series and parallel circuits, showing switch, battery, loads/resistors, ammeter, and voltmeter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions series resistors but does not instruct drawing or assembling circuits, nor does it mention switch, battery, ammeter, or voltmeter. It shares vocabulary but gives no direct support for the drawing/assembly skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ever wonder how Christmas lights share the same current?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: collaborate in a class discussion to recognize the advantages and limitations of using series or parallel circuits
assignedReviews.reason: The Christmas lights example hints at a series-circuit behavior, but the card does not discuss advantages or limitations of series vs parallel circuits, nor does it support a class discussion on that topic.

copy.en:
Ever wonder how Christmas lights share the same current?

When resistors are in series (in a row), you add their resistances to get the total, then apply Ohm's law. The same current flows through every part!
copy.tl:
Naisip mo ba kung paano nagkakapareho ang kuryente sa Christmas lights?

Kapag magkasunod (series) ang mga resistor, pinagsasama ang kanilang resistensya para makuha ang kabuuan, tapos gamitin ang batas ni Ohm. Pareho ang kuryente sa lahat ng bahagi!
copy.bis:
Nainglan ka ba unsaon pag-share sa Christmas lights sa parehas nga kuryente?

Kung gisunod-sunod (series) ang mga resistor, idugang ang ilang resistensya aron makuha ang total, dayon gamita ang balaod ni Ohm. Parehas ang kuryente sa tanang bahin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: when a wire heats up, its resistance goes up
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that resistance changes with temperature, which is a factor affecting resistance, but the competency requires guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits. The card does not address circuit assembly, current, voltage, or the Ohm's law relationship directly; it only notes a condition under which Ohm's law is exact.

copy.en: Does resistance change? Yes! In most metals, when a wire heats up, its resistance goes up. That's why Ohm's law is most exact when the temperature stays the same!
copy.tl: Nagbabago ba ang resistance? Oo! Sa karamihan ng metals, kapag umiinit ang wire, tumataas ang resistance nito. Kaya ang Ohm's law ay pinakatumpak kapag pare-pareho ang temperature!
copy.bis: Mausab ba ang resistance? Oo! Sa kadaghanan sa metals, kung moinit ang wire, mosaka ang resistance niini. Mao nga ang Ohm's law pinakatukma kung parehas ang temperature!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A thicker wire has less resistance, so current flows more easily!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about wire thickness and resistance, but does not address the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series or parallel circuits, nor does it involve guided investigation or varying loads/battery. It is only tangentially related to resistance.

copy.en:
Why are some cables made thick?

A thicker wire has less resistance, so current flows more easily! A long, thin wire has more resistance. That's exactly why some cables are made thick!
copy.tl:
Bakit may mga kable na makapal?

Ang mas makapal na wire ay may mas kaunting resistance, kaya mas madaling dumaloy ang current! Ang mahaba at manipis na wire ay may mas maraming resistance. Kaya makapal ang ibang kable!
copy.bis:
Nganong naay mga kable nga baga?

Ang mas baga nga wire adunay mas ubos nga resistance, busa mas sayon moagas ang current! Ang taas ug nipis nga wire adunay mas daghan nga resistance. Mao nga baga ang ubang kable!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Voltage is in volts, current in amperes (amps), and resistance in ohms!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the units for voltage, current, and resistance. It does not support the competency's action of participating in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled circuits. Knowing the units is useful background for such investigations but does not directly teach the relationship or the investigation process.

copy.en:
What are the units in Ohm's law?

Voltage is in volts, current in amperes (amps), and resistance in ohms! The ohm symbol is the Greek letter omega (Ω).
copy.tl:
Ano ang mga yunit sa batas ni Ohm?

Ang boltahe ay nasa volt, kuryente sa ampere (amp), at resistensya sa ohm! Ang simbolo ng ohm ay ang letrang Griyego na omega (Ω).
copy.bis:
Unsa ang mga yunit sa balaod ni Ohm?

Ang boltahe nasa volt, kuryente sa ampere (amp), ug resistensya sa ohm! Ang simbolo sa ohm kay ang Griyegong letra nga omega (Ω).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Voltage is the pressure pushing it, current is the water flowing, and resistance is a narrow pipe slowing the flow.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card presents a water-pipe analogy for voltage, current, and resistance, but the competency requires participating in guided investigations to infer the relationship among these quantities in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying loads and battery. The card does not mention circuits, series/parallel arrangements, loads, batteries, or any investigation, so it only shares vocabulary/concepts without directly supporting the stated skill.

copy.en: Picture water in a pipe! Voltage is the pressure pushing it, current is the water flowing, and resistance is a narrow pipe slowing the flow.
copy.tl: Isipin ang tubig sa tubo! Ang boltahe ay presyong nagtutulak, ang kuryente ay dami ng tubig na dumadaloy, at ang resistensya ay makitid na tumutigil sa daloy.
copy.bis: Hunahunaa ang tubig sa tubo! Ang boltahe kay presyon nga nagtulod, ang kuryente kay gidaghanon sa tubig nga nagaagas, ug ang resistensya kay sip-on nga tubo nga nagpahinay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Adding soap makes oil stop floating and mix with water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an everyday example of soap helping oil mix with water (an emulsion), but it does not describe the mixture as uniform or non-uniform, nor does it mention solutions or suspensions. It only shows a practical effect without classifying the mixture type, so it does not directly support the competency's skill of describing uniform vs non-uniform mixtures.

copy.en: Adding soap makes oil stop floating and mix with water! That’s why we use soap on greasy plates—it breaks oil into tiny pieces water can wash away!
copy.tl: Kapag nilagyan ng soap, humihinto ang oil sa paglutang at nahahalo sa tubig! Kaya naghuhugas tayo ng mamantikang pinggan—pinaghihiwalay ito ng oil para madaling mahugas!
copy.bis: Kung butangan og soap, mohunong ang oil sa paglutaw ug magsagol sa tubig! Mao nga manghugas tag sabon sa mantikaon nga plato—gibungkag niini ang oil aron dali mahanas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you'll find a slimy inside packed with tiny seeds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Seeds inside a sliced okra are fruit anatomy/food, not pollination, seed production, or plant propagation as methods.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Slice open an okra and you'll find a slimy inside packed with tiny seeds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: Okra interior is not leaves, roots, or stems taking water and nutrients from soil.

copy.en: Slice open an okra and you'll find a slimy inside packed with tiny seeds!
copy.tl: Kapag hiniwa ang okra, malagkit ang laman nito at puno ng maliliit na buto!
copy.bis: Kung hiwaon ang okra, lapot ang sulod ug puno kini sa gagmayng liso!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PAGASA now uses the name Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal. It's the exact same family of numbers as the older Public Storm Warning Signal in your textbooks!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geological and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only notes the renaming of the signal and that the number family is the same. It does not describe any weather conditions associated with the signal, which is the core action of the competency.

copy.en: PAGASA now uses the name Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal. It's the exact same family of numbers as the older Public Storm Warning Signal in your textbooks!
copy.tl: Gumagamit na ngayon ang PAGASA ng pangalang Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal. Ito ang mismong pamilya ng numero tulad ng lumang Public Storm Warning Signal sa mga aklat!
copy.bis: Naggamit na karon ang PAGASA sa ngalan nga Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal. Kini ang samang pamilya sa numero sama sa daan nga Public Storm Warning Signal sa mga libro!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: old mountains are rounded and smooth from long erosion
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions erosion as the cause of rounded old mountains, but it does not demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials. It only states a result of erosion, not the process of transport.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Young mountains are sharp and steep, while old mountains are rounded and smooth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to mountains as landforms but does not identify local examples or describe how they influence living and non-living components of the environment. It only describes a general difference between young and old mountains.

copy.en: Young mountains are sharp and steep, while old mountains are rounded and smooth from long erosion!
copy.tl: Ang mga batang bundok ay matulis at matarik, habang ang matatandang bundok ay mas bilog at pantay!
copy.bis: Ang mga bata pa nga bukid talinis ug tarik, samtang ang tigulang nga bukid mas lingin ug hamis!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Methuselah, the world's oldest tree, grows quietly in the White Mountains of California, standing for thousands of years.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the location and age of a single tree. It does not compare life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants from seed to mature plant, which is the required competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Methuselah, the world's oldest tree, grows quietly in the White Mountains of California, standing for thousands of years.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that the tree grows, but it does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It is a trivia fact about a specific tree's location and age, not an instructional description of growth as a characteristic.

copy.en:
Where does the oldest tree grow?

Methuselah, the world's oldest tree, grows quietly in the White Mountains of California, standing for thousands of years.
copy.tl:
Saan tumutubo ang pinakamatandang puno?

Ang Methuselah, ang pinakamatandang puno sa mundo, ay tumutubo sa White Mountains ng California, tumatayo na nang libu-libong taon.
copy.bis:
Asa motubo ang pinakatigulang kahoy?

Ang Methuselah, ang pinakatigulang kahoy sa kalibutan, motubo sa White Mountains sa California, nagbarog na sa liboan ka tuig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An omnivore eats both plants and animals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines omnivore and gives examples, but does not group animals into herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores, nor does it use secondary sources. It only touches one category of the grouping skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An omnivore eats both plants and animals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw a simple food chain using living things from the Philippines and label them as herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not draw a food chain, does not use Philippine living things, and does not label herbivores/carnivores/omnivores. It only defines omnivore, which is background vocabulary for the required drawn food chain.

copy.en:
What is an omnivore?

An omnivore eats both plants and animals — that includes people, pigs, and chickens!
copy.tl:
Ano ang omnivore?

Ang omnivore ay kumakain ng halaman at hayop — kasama dito ang tao, baboy, at manok!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang omnivore?

Ang omnivore mokaon og tanom ug hayop — apil dinhi ang tawo, baboy, ug manok!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: an omnivore can eat animals; when animals are scarce, it eats plants instead
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only discusses omnivores and their flexible diet, but does not teach grouping animals into herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores, nor does it use secondary sources as required by the competency.

copy.en: When plants are scarce, an omnivore can eat animals; when animals are scarce, it eats plants instead. This flexible diet helps omnivores survive even when the season or food supply changes.
copy.tl: Kapag kaunti ang halaman, kumakain ng hayop ang omnivore; kapag kaunti naman ang hayop, kumakain ito ng halaman. Dahil sa flexible na diyeta na ito, mas madali silang mabuhay kahit magbago ang panahon o ang available na pagkain.
copy.bis: Kung gamay ang tanom, mokaon og hayop ang omnivore; kung gamay ang hayop, mokaon kini og tanom. Tungod sa flexible nga pagkaon niini, mas sayon silang mabuhi bisan magbag-o ang panahon o ang makaplagan nga pagkaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: we mix plant foods like bran or veggies with protein like meat or fish — just like their natural diet!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that pigs and dogs naturally eat both plants and meat, which hints at omnivory, but it does not name the categories herbivore, carnivore, omnivore, nor does it group animals according to the food they eat. It only gives a single example of a mixed diet without the classification action required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: we mix plant foods like bran or veggies with protein like meat or fish
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about what we feed pets, not about identifying the basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter). Food is mentioned as part of the diet, but the card does not teach that food is a basic need or address the other basic needs. It is only tangentially related to the concept of food as a need.

copy.en: When we feed a pig or dog, we mix plant foods like bran or veggies with protein like meat or fish — just like their natural diet!
copy.tl: Kapag pinapakain natin ang baboy o aso, hinahalo natin ang halaman tulad ng darak o gulay at protina tulad ng karne o isda — gaya ng kanilang likas na pagkain!
copy.bis: Kung pakan-on nato ang baboy o iro, sagolan nato ang tanom sama sa tahup o utanon ug protina sama sa karne o isda — sama sa ilang natural nga pagkaon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Opal is silica that contains some water, giving it a shifting play of colors!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a rock/mineral (opal) but does not involve exploring or collecting rocks, nor comparing different rocks by texture, color, or grain crystal size. It only gives a fact about opal's composition and color play.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Opal is silica that contains some water, giving it a shifting play of colors!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on a visual/optical feature of a solid material, but it does not describe physical properties such as hard, shiny, or stretchable, nor does it support the competency's focus on describing physical properties of solid materials.

copy.en:
What makes an opal shift in beautiful colors?

Opal is silica that contains some water, giving it a shifting play of colors!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagpapabago-bago sa kulay ng opal?

Ang opal ay silica na may lamang tubig, kaya nagbabago-bago ang kulay nitong sumisinag!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang nagpabalin-balhin sa kolor sa opal?

Ang opal mao ang silica nga adunay tubig, mao nga nagbalhinbalhin ang kolor niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A planet's speed must be just right — too slow and it falls in, too fast and it flies away!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses orbital speed balance for planets but does not explicitly describe gravity or its effect on the motion of an object. It only implies gravitational attraction indirectly through falling/flying away, so it does not directly support observing/describing gravity's effects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A planet's speed must be just right — too slow and it falls in, too fast and it flies away!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not define speed as distance over time or identify how far an object moves in a given time. It only mentions that a planet's speed must be 'just right,' which is unrelated to the G4-F-3 competency about measuring and identifying speed.

copy.en:
Why don't planets fall into the Sun or fly away?

A planet's speed must be just right — too slow and it falls in, too fast and it flies away!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi nahuhulog ang mga planeta sa Araw o lumilipad palayo?

Kailangan tama lang ang bilis ng planeta — kung sobrang bagal, mahuhulog ito sa Araw; kung sobrang bilis, lilipad ito palayo.
copy.bis:
Ngano dili mahulog ang mga planeta sa Adlaw o molupad palayo?

Ang katulin sa planeta kinahanglan saktong-sakto — kon sobra ka hinay, mahulog kini sa Adlaw; kon sobra ka paspas, molupad kini palayo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they don't steal any food from the tree
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: Not stealing food is not explaining how an interaction brings good or harm.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many orchids grow right on tree branches
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many orchids grow right on tree branches, but don't worry — they don't steal any food from the tree
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not how living things depend on one another to meet their basic needs.

copy.en: Many orchids grow right on tree branches, but don't worry — they don't steal any food from the tree.
copy.tl: Maraming orkidya ang tumutubo mismo sa mga sanga ng puno, pero huwag mag-alala — hindi nila kinukuha ang sustansya ng puno.
copy.bis: Daghang orkid ang motubo direkta sa mga sanga sa kahoy, apan ayaw kabalaka — dili nila kuhaon ang sustansya sa kahoy.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most orchids prefer soft light and shade, not the harsh direct rays of the sun.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a plant (orchid) and light, but it does not describe orchids as biotic factors or light as an abiotic factor. It only states a light preference, which is not the classification or description required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most orchids prefer soft light and shade, not the harsh direct rays of the sun.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how some plants have adapted to unfavorable conditions in the environment, such as lack of rain or floods
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a light preference, not an adaptation to unfavorable conditions such as lack of rain or floods. Shade preference is not an example of adapting to unfavorable conditions in the sense of the competency.

copy.en: Most orchids prefer soft light and shade, not the harsh direct rays of the sun.
copy.tl: Karamihan sa orkidya ay gusto ng malamlam na liwanag at lilim, hindi ang matinding sinag ng araw.
copy.bis: Kadaghanan sa mga orkid gusto og humok nga kahayag ug landong, dili ang hilabihang silaw sa adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most ore has very little gold!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions gold as a metal found in ore; it does not identify properties or uses of metals such as gold, iron, silver, or copper.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: we have to process several tons of rock just to get enough gold
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers generally to processing rock to obtain gold, but it does not demonstrate or describe any specific mixture separation technique such as decantation, filtering, sieving, or using magnets.

copy.en: Most ore has very little gold! Sometimes, we have to process several tons of rock just to get enough gold for a single ring.
copy.tl: Napakakaunti ng ginto sa karamihang ore! Kailangan minsang magproseso ng ilang tonelada ng bato para makakuha ng sapat na ginto para sa isang singsing.
copy.bis: Gamay ra kaayo ang bulawan sa kadaghanang ore! Usahay kinahanglang prosesohon ang pila ka tonelada nga bato aron makakuha og igong bulawan para sa usa ka singsing.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An ore's 'grade' tells how much metal is inside!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains ore grade (metal content in ore). It does not describe uniform or non-uniform mixtures, solutions, or suspensions, nor any everyday mixture examples. The topic is unrelated to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An ore's 'grade' tells how much metal is inside!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: express quantitatively the amount of solute present in a given volume of solvent
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses metal concentration in ore, not the amount of solute in a given volume of solvent. No solute, solvent, or quantitative concentration concept is taught. Unrelated to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An ore's 'grade' tells how much metal is inside!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some useful things that people have made from non-living materials and describe what natural materials have been used to make the items
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not identify useful things made from non-living materials or describe natural materials used to make items. It only defines ore grade, which is not covered by this competency.

copy.en: An ore's 'grade' tells how much metal is inside! High-grade ore has lots of metal, making it worth mining, while low-grade ore has very little.
copy.tl: Ang 'grade' ng ore ay nagsasabi kung gaano karaming metal ang nasa loob! Ang high-grade ore ay maraming metal, habang ang low-grade ay konti lang.
copy.bis: Ang 'grade' sa ore nagpasabot kung pila ka metal ang sulod! Ang high-grade nga ore daghan og metal, samtang ang low-grade gamay ra.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most of the world's iron and steel are actually made from this amazing rock.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions iron as a metal and that hematite is used to make iron/steel, but it does not identify properties of metals (e.g., hardness, conductivity) or their uses in the local community as the competency requires. assignedReviews.card_evidence: A common example of ore is hematite, a reddish rock full of iron!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card names hematite as a reddish rock, touching on color, but it does not involve exploring, observing, or collecting different types of rocks, nor comparing similarities/differences in texture, color, or grain crystal size. It provides no instructional support for the rock observation/classification skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most of the world's iron and steel are actually made from this amazing rock.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some useful things that people have made from non-living materials and describe what natural materials have been used to make the items
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that iron and steel are made from hematite, which is a useful product made from a non-living material. The support is too indirect for this competency.

copy.en: A common example of ore is hematite, a reddish rock full of iron! Most of the world's iron and steel are actually made from this amazing rock.
copy.tl: Isang karaniwang halimbawa ng ore ay ang hematite, isang mapula-pulang bato na puno ng iron! Mula rito ginagawa ang karamihan ng bakal at asero sa buong mundo.
copy.bis: Usa ka kasagarang pananglitan sa ore mao ang hematite, usa ka mapula-pula nga bato nga puno sa puthaw! Gikan niini gihimo ang kadaghanan sa puthaw ug asero sa tibuok kalibotan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is just rock with metal mixed in
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a mixture (rock with metal mixed in) but does not describe uniform vs non-uniform mixtures, nor give examples like solutions and suspensions. It does not directly support the competency's skill of describing useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures.

Ang oxygen naglangkob sa mga 21% sa hangin! Kini ang ikaduhang pinakadaghang gas niini.

copy.en: Oxygen makes up about 21% of the air in Earth's atmosphere!
copy.tl: Ang oxygen (oksiheno) ay bumubuo ng mga 21% ng hangin sa atmosphere ng Earth!
copy.bis: Ang oxygen (oksiheno) naglangkob og mga 21% sa hangin sa atmospera sa Yuta!

copy.en: Oxygen makes things burn brighter and faster! That’s why a glowing splint suddenly flares up with a big flame when placed in pure oxygen.
copy.tl: Pinalalakas ng oxygen ang pagkasunog! Kaya kapag inilubog ang nag-aapoy na patpat sa pure oxygen, biglang lumalakas ang liyab nito.
copy.bis: Gipakusog sa oxygen ang pagsunog! Mao nga kung ituslob ang nagbaga nga sungkod sa lunsay nga oxygen, kalit kining mosiga og dako nga liyab.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is oxygen! This is the special gas in the air that helps things burn
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor

copy.en:
What gas in the air helps things burn?

It is oxygen! This is the special gas in the air that helps things burn and supports the fire.
copy.tl:
Anong gas sa hangin ang tumutulong sa pagliyab ng apoy?

Ito ay oxygen! Ang espesyal na gas sa hangin na tumutulong sa pagliyab ng apoy ay itong gas na oxygen.
copy.bis:
Unsa nga gas sa hangin ang motabang sa pagdilaab sa kalayo?

Oksiheno ang tubag! Ang gas sa hangin nga motabang sa pagdilaab sa kalayo mao niining espesyal nga gas nga oksiheno.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Oxygen makes up about 21% of the air we breathe!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions oxygen as a component of air but does not describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor. It only gives a single fact about oxygen percentage, not the full mixture description required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's essential for both fire and life — without oxygen, flames can't burn and animals can't survive.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card states oxygen is essential for life, but the competency is about identifying basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter). The card does not teach that air is a basic need; it only mentions oxygen's role in survival, which is background rather than direct instruction on identifying basic needs.

copy.en: Oxygen makes up about 21% of the air we breathe! It's essential for both fire and life — without oxygen, flames can't burn and animals can't survive.
copy.tl: Ang oxygen ay bumubuo ng mga 21% ng hangin! Mahalaga ito sa pagsusunog at paghinga — kung wala ang oxygen, mamamatay ang apoy at ang mga hayop.
copy.bis: Ang oxygen nagbubuo sa mga 21% sa hangin! Kini importante sa pagsunog ug paghinga — kung walay oxygen, dili makasunog ang kalayo ug dili mabuhi ang mga hayop.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Oxygen is the gas that helps things burn!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how important types of chemical reactions, such as combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, and respiration, relate to or impact the natural and built environments using information from secondary sources

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions oxygen as a gas but does not describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor. It only gives a property of oxygen, not the composition of air.

copy.en: Oxygen is the gas that helps things burn! When a flame uses up all the oxygen around it, poof — the flame goes out!
copy.tl: Ang oxygen ang gas na tumutulong sa mga bagay na masunog! Kapag naubos na ang oxygen paligid ng apoy, poof — mamatay na ito!
copy.bis: Ang oxygen mao ang gas nga nagtabang nga masunog ang mga butang! Kung mahurot na ang oxygen palibot sa kalayo, poof — mapalong na kini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fire needs oxygen to burn brightly!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions oxygen as a requirement for burning. It does not describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fire needs oxygen to burn brightly!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how important types of chemical reactions, such as combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, and respiration, relate to or impact the natural and built environments using information from secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on combustion needing oxygen, but it does not explain how combustion relates to or impacts the natural and built environments, nor does it use secondary sources. It is only a basic statement about burning.

copy.en: Fire needs oxygen to burn brightly! If the oxygen is cut off, the flame will quickly go out.
copy.tl: Kailangan ng oxygen para magliyab ang apoy! Kapag wala nito, ang apoy ay mabilis na mamamatay.
copy.bis: Nagkinahanglan og oxihena ang kalayo aron modilaab! Kon walay oxihena, paspas kini mapalong.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Up high in the stratosphere, it blocks harmful UV rays.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that stratospheric ozone blocks UV rays, which is an example of solar energy interacting with the atmosphere, but it does not explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere in general. The focus is on good vs bad ozone, not on the mechanisms of Sun-atmosphere interaction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: But near the ground, pollution makes ozone that hurts our lungs!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain the harmful effects that EMR can have on living things
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that ground-level ozone from pollution hurts lungs, which is a harmful effect on living things, but it does not explain harmful effects of electromagnetic radiation (EMR) on living things. Ozone is a gas, not EMR, and the card does not address EMR.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: But near the ground, pollution makes ozone that hurts our lungs!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe the possible effects of human activities, such as deforestation, pollution, and introduction of invasive species, on living things in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions pollution creating harmful ozone, which relates to human activities affecting living things, but it does not describe possible effects of human activities such as deforestation, pollution, or invasive species on living things in an ecosystem. The statement is too brief and lacks ecosystem context.

copy.en: Did you know ozone can be good OR bad? Up high in the stratosphere, it blocks harmful UV rays. But near the ground, pollution makes ozone that hurts our lungs!
copy.tl: Alam mo bang may mabuti at masamang ozone? Sa itaas sa stratosphere, hinaharang nito ang UV. Pero sa lupa, may ozone mula sa polusyon na nakakasama sa baga!
copy.bis: Nahibaw-an ba ka nga naay maayo ug daotang ozone? Sa taas sa stratosphere, gibabagan niini ang UV. Apan duol sa yuta, naay ozone gikan sa polusyon nga makadaot sa baga!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Countries agreed to stop using harmful CFC chemicals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an environmental success story (ozone recovery from CFC ban) but does not directly teach the need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive. It is related to environmental protection but lacks explicit instruction on conservation for living things.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ozone layer is slowly healing
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local impacts of global climate change and suggest ways that individuals can do to reduce the impact of global warming
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions ozone layer recovery, which is an environmental issue, but does not identify local impacts of global climate change or suggest individual actions to reduce global warming. Ozone depletion is distinct from climate change, and no local impacts or individual mitigation suggestions are provided.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Countries agreed to stop using harmful CFC chemicals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate ways to minimize harmful changes in materials, such as restriction of burning of waste materials, and care in handling reactive materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions stopping harmful CFC chemicals, which relates to minimizing harmful changes in materials, but it does not demonstrate ways to minimize harmful changes in materials (e.g., restriction of burning waste, care in handling reactive materials). It is a general example of reducing harmful substances, not a demonstration of the competency.

copy.en: Good news! The ozone layer is slowly healing. Countries agreed to stop using harmful CFC chemicals, and now the ozone is slowly getting thicker again over the years.
copy.tl: Magandang balita! Dahan-dahang gumagaling ang ozone layer. Nagkasundo ang mga bansa na ihinto ang paggamit ng CFC chemicals, kaya unti-unting bumabalik ang kapal ng ozone.
copy.bis: Maayong balita! Hinay-hinay nga naghapit maayo ang ozone layer. Nagkasabot ang mga nasod nga undangon ang paggamit sa CFC chemicals, mao nga hinay-hinay nga mibalik ang kabaga sa ozone.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ozone is made of three oxygen atoms joined together (O3)
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes ozone as a molecule of three oxygen atoms and contrasts it with O2. It does not address pure substances, fixed chemical composition, elements versus compounds, or the unique number of protons in atoms of an element. The content is only tangentially related to atomic/molecular composition.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The air we breathe has oxygen with only two atoms (O2)
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions oxygen in the air but does not describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor. It only contrasts O2 with O3, so it does not directly support the competency's focus on air as a mixture of specific gases.

copy.en: Ozone is made of three oxygen atoms joined together (O3). The air we breathe has oxygen with only two atoms (O2) — so ozone is different from ordinary oxygen!
copy.tl: Ang ozone ay gawa sa tatlong atom ng oxygen na magkakabit (O3). Ang hangin na nilalanghap natin ay may oxygen na dalawang atom lang (O2) — kaya iba ang ozone sa ordinaryong oxygen!
copy.bis: Ang ozone hinimo sa tulo ka atom sa oxygen nga nagdugtong (O3). Ang hangin nga atong ginaginhawa adunay oxygen nga duha ra ka atom (O2) — mao nga lahi ang ozone sa ordinaryong oxygen!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ozone blocks the most dangerous UV rays from reaching the ground
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe safety measures that people can use to avoid the harmful effects of the Sun's light
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that ozone blocks dangerous UV rays and that weaker UV burns skin, but it does not describe any safety measures people can use to avoid harmful effects of the Sun's light (e.g., sunscreen, hats, limiting exposure). It only provides background about UV radiation, so it is related but not directly supporting the competency.

copy.en: Ozone blocks the most dangerous UV rays from reaching the ground! The weaker type gets through, which is what burns your skin after long hours in the sun.
copy.tl: Halos buong hinaharang ng ozone ang pinakadelikadong UV bago makarating sa lupa! Ang mas mahinang uri ay nakakalusot, kaya iyon ang nakakapaso sa balat kapag matagal sa araw.
copy.bis: Halos hingpit nga gibabagan sa ozone ang labing peligroso nga UV! Ang mas huyang nga matang makalusot, ug mao kana ang makapaso sa panit kung dugay sa adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: global warming is about trapped heat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify evidence of global warming and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions global warming as trapped heat; it does not identify any evidence of global warming or climate change, such as temperature records, ice melt, or sea-level rise.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: global warming is about trapped heat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of greenhouse gases in enhanced global warming and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to trapped heat, which is a general idea related to greenhouse warming, but it does not identify the role of specific greenhouse gases or explain enhanced global warming.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ozone is about UV rays
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions UV rays and ozone, which relate to solar energy interacting with the atmosphere, but it does not explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere; it only contrasts ozone depletion with global warming.

copy.en: The ozone hole and global warming are two different problems! Ozone is about UV rays, while global warming is about trapped heat.
copy.tl: Magkaibang problema ang butas sa ozone at global warming! Ang ozone ay tungkol sa UV rays, samantalang ang global warming ay tungkol sa naiipong init.
copy.bis: Lahi nga problema ang lungag sa ozone ug global warming! Ang ozone bahin sa UV rays, samtang ang global warming bahin sa natipon nga init.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: so our ozone layer and sun protection matter a lot!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe safety measures that people can use to avoid the harmful effects of the Sun's light
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sun protection and high UV but does not describe any specific safety measures people can use to avoid the harmful effects of the Sun's light.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: so our ozone layer and sun protection matter a lot!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how light and sound can be harmful to people and make suggestions on how to protect oneself from them
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to high UV and sun protection but does not explain how light is harmful or make suggestions for protecting oneself from light or sound.

copy.en:
Why do we need extra sun protection in the Philippines?

We are near the equator with a high UV index, so our ozone layer and sun protection matter a lot!
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangan natin ng extra sun protection sa Pilipinas?

Malapit tayo sa equator at mataas ang UV index, kaya mahalaga ang ozone layer at sun protection natin!
copy.bis:
Nganong kinahanglan og extra sun protection sa Pilipinas?

Duol kita sa equator ug taas ang UV index, busa importante kaayo ang ozone layer ug sun protection nato!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: By filtering UV rays, the ozone layer protects us from sunburn, skin cancer, and eye damage!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how light and sound can be harmful to people and make suggestions on how to protect oneself from them
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that UV light can be harmful (sunburn, skin cancer, eye damage) but does not make suggestions on how to protect oneself from light or sound. The ozone layer is presented as the protective mechanism, not personal safety measures. Thus it only partially touches the harmful aspect without the required protective suggestions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: By filtering UV rays, the ozone layer protects us from sunburn, skin cancer, and eye damage!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe safety measures that people can use to avoid the harmful effects of the Sun's light
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the ozone layer's role in filtering UV rays, which relates to avoiding harmful effects of the Sun's light, but it does not describe safety measures that people can use (e.g., sunscreen, hats, sunglasses). The protective action is attributed to the ozone layer, not to personal safety measures, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How does the ozone layer keep our bodies safe?

By filtering UV rays, the ozone layer protects us from sunburn, skin cancer, and eye damage!
copy.tl:
Paano tayo pinoprotektahan ng ozone layer?

Sa pagsala ng UV, pinoprotektahan tayo ng ozone layer laban sa sunburn, skin cancer, at eye damage!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpanalipod sa ozone layer sa atong lawas?

Pinaagi sa pagsala sa UV, ang ozone layer manalipod kanato batok sa sunburn, skin cancer, ug eye damage!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it would only be a few millimeters thick.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe different science process skills used in performing simple science activities, such as observing, predicting, and measuring using units such as millimeter, centimeter, and meter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the unit 'millimeters' but does not describe science process skills such as observing, predicting, or measuring, nor how to use units in simple science activities.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ozone is super important but very thin!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions ozone, which is part of the atmosphere, but does not explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere. It only states that ozone is thin, with no discussion of solar energy or atmospheric interaction.

copy.en: Ozone is super important but very thin! If gathered at ground level, it would only be a few millimeters thick.
copy.tl: Napakahalaga ng ozone pero napakanipis! Kung titipunin sa ground level, mga ilang millimeters lang ang kapal.
copy.bis: Importante kaayo ang ozone pero nipis kaayo! Kung tipikon sa ground level, pipila lang ka millimeters ang gibag-on.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes reflection of light in a concave mirror, which is unrelated to the competency about how sound is made and transferred. The topic is light, not sound.

copy.en: A light ray traveling parallel to the principal axis reflects through the focal point in a concave mirror.
copy.tl: Ang light ray na parallel sa principal axis ay nagre-reflect papunta sa focal point sa concave mirror.
copy.bis: Ang light ray nga parallel sa principal axis mo-reflect padulong sa focal point sa concave mirror.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There are five tropical cyclone wind signals, from Signal No. 1 to Signal No. 5. The higher the number, the stronger the wind!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geological and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the number of wind signal levels and that higher numbers mean stronger winds. It does not describe the specific weather conditions (e.g., wind speed ranges, expected impacts) associated with each Public Storm Warning Signal, which is the core of the competency.

copy.en:
How many wind signal levels does PAGASA use for typhoons?

There are five tropical cyclone wind signals, from Signal No. 1 to Signal No. 5. The higher the number, the stronger the wind!
copy.tl:
Ilan ang antas ng wind signal na ginagamit ng PAGASA para sa bagyo?

May limang tropical cyclone wind signal, mula Signal No. 1 hanggang Signal No. 5. Mas mataas ang numero, mas malakas ang hangin!
copy.bis:
Pila ka ang-ang sa wind signal ang gigamit sa PAGASA para sa bagyo?

Adunay lima ka tropical cyclone wind signal, gikan Signal No. 1 hangtod Signal No. 5. Mas taas ang numero, mas kusog ang hangin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The highest is Signal No. 5, raised when a super typhoon is coming!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geological and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the highest signal number and that it is used for super typhoons. It does not describe the weather conditions (e.g., wind speed, rainfall) associated with any Public Storm Warning Signal, which is the core action of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: raised when a super typhoon is coming!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a super typhoon 'coming' but does not describe typical weather conditions before, during, or after a tropical cyclone. It only gives a single fact about signal assignment, not the required weather descriptions.

copy.en:
What's the highest storm signal PAGASA can raise?

The highest is Signal No. 5, raised when a super typhoon is coming!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamataas na storm signal na itinataas ng PAGASA?

Ang pinakamataas ay Signal No. 5, itinataas para sa super typhoon!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakataas nga storm signal nga ipataas sa PAGASA?

Ang pinakataas mao ang Signal No. 5, ipataas para sa super typhoon!
